[b][u]Internal Chaos on Empire Island[/u][/b]
As soon as the communications on Empire Island began to be shaky, chaos soon erupted. Evacuation from the island was too late for safety to be a present factor for evacuation ships and planes. It would be estimated that within the time between the initial attacks and a land invasion/complete encirclement of Empire Island around 10% (approx 500k) of the population of Empire Island could be evacuated in some form. Many valuable assets and important figureheads were among the first to board evacuation ships and planes at the largest city on the island, Port Augustus. 

Surprisingly, the island was relatively calm and even resilient as the attack which had be speculated to occur soon, had happened just right now. The militia which had been estimated to be conscripting 600k men has begun to organise and train these conscripts. So far around 120k conscripts have been formed into recognisable military units which have been put around the island to help bolster existing land forces, with a further 200k in their formation and training stage. Existing factories on the island have mostly been reprimanded for production of military equipment and materials, most notable of which are cheap drones and missiles which are readily able to be used against air and naval invasion.

For the civilians, they are taught firstly to be prepared to deal with the spread of HIV and AIDs from Gaesunian forces if they launch a land invasion. Then mass construction of bunkers which are soon to be utilised for civilian protection against air raids and urban warfare have set in a tone of total war amongst the minds of Empire Islanders. Food rations have also been put in place along with a curfew of people doing nighttime activities to prevent enemies having a good ariel view of the island's infrastructure. 

The local Adamites, who number around a million followers on the island have decided that peace and love are the main objective to settle this issue once and for all. Departing from their "love ports", they head towards all directions from the island in order to meet with the Gaesunian naval forces to convince them to act peaceful and join in celebrations of love with Balionic forces. With their open deck wooden ships, adorned with peace, love and simple Christian symbols with the men and women crews commandeering the ships in their full ritual attire, it is considered by the anti-war crowd to be a last ditch effort to stop the war.

[b]Hearing the news[/b]

A man briskly walked down the streets of St. Douglass, maybe headed to work, maybe headed for a bite of famed Aceldix barbecue or a coffee made out of horse dung or something, whatever it may be. He took a left on a street labeled Greenshill and saw the newspaper stand. Quickly checking in his pocket for money, he walked up to the stand and asked whats new. He was handed his paper, and after paying the man at the stand generously, he spotted himself an empty bench.

The title of the paper read in bold letters, [b]Whitney Massacre[/b]. But Aceldix had not fought a war since its bloody secession war with the Erene Federation, he thought. What do you mean massacre?

He read on:
On the 15th of January, near the city of Whitney, the 16th Aceldixan Armored Battalion came in contact with a mysterious mech and commenced fire upon the unknown intruder. 

This came after a large sized ship appeared out of our atmosphere and released a shuttle into our moon. The ship apparently had no visible markings, badges or flags of identification, signaling that it was perhaps pirates or a lost vessel from a foreign country. The only thing that was seen was that it was a Federation design.

The mech was defeated by the overwhelming force within a matter of minutes via a tank shot on critical areas of the machine. After being shot down, the driver self-destructed and destroyed much of the wreckage of the mech. Oddly enough, the mech contained no markings or identification on who it belonged to. The battalion suffered moderate damage from the mech, but aside from 2 cars it was nothing that couldnt be repaired, according to some of the crew of the battalion.

The mech was previously wreaking havoc on the mining facility at which the battle took place, destroying key infrastructure and causing major casualties and loss of life to the miners within. About 63 confirmed casualties were recorded in the event, a tragic loss of life for our home of Aceldix.

Several thoughts were running through the mans mind. Who was responsible for this?

A photograph of the wreckage of the mech was taken and posted in the newspaper. The man inspected it carefully, for he noticed something strange. Were those runes?

[i]How? What reason would Palleon have to spark a war with Aceldama? No, wait, this doesnt make any sense. If they really were planning to wage war with Aceldama, they wouldnt have sent just a mech. They wouldve sent an army, if they had the nerve to even invade a land like Aceldama. Hmm.

Maybe Korrin? Wait. No. Thats the dumbest one yet. They declared independence from the Erene Federation mere weeks ago. They wouldnt start conflict with a neutral nation in their goal of independence, thats stupid. Beyond stupid. No, its not them.

Maybe the Erene Federation itself? Hmm. Yes, yes, it could. If the ship was a Federation design, and the mech was unmarked, then perhaps it was them. Combined with the recent Korrin uprising, they could be trying to false flag us. Interesting.[/i]

He looked at the time. It was time to go, maybe even a little well past time. He stood up from his bench and continued strolling down the sidewalk, if maybe with a little kick in his pace.

Blood, ash, mangled metal on a flat ground, like disjointed iconography of an absurdist art piece. 

It was just like Aceldama. Just a few minutes after landing, and the area around NSI3-5's mobile suit was now a land of utter destruction. However, thanks to lessons learned from NSI3-4's overly ambitious approach, NSI3-5 moved cautiously, hiding its mobile suit in the rubble of its own making like makeshift sandbags to coneal and protect itself from the gradually overwhelming Illynite reponse.

The Wardens' 25mm kinetic penetrators would be insufficient to harm Frame 167, whose heavy composite armor would easily absorb, if not outright shatter the darts on contact. That was, if they could hit at all, with NSI3-5 having been wise to keep its ballistic shield on its rear, where the Wardens' projectile fire would be met and checked by a gigantic wall of 30mm silicon carbide ceramic backed by 100mm of ballistic steel.

[LIST]"So Illynites have been mass producing mechtech too..." NSI3-5 said, furrowing her eyebrows as barrage after barrage of depleted uranium penetrators crashed against the thick shield of the Frame 167, each bursting impact causing the clone to jump from shock. "... ineffective in the mean time though, I should be g-..."[/LIST]

Just then, NSI3-5's words are cut off by a sudden, destructive blast that staggers the mobile suit, causing it to almost tumble down to the ground, though MSI3-5 saves itself, grabbing onto a shattered dome to slow its fall. A well-aimed tank shell had hit Frame 167's lower torso, causing some of its mobility thrusters and fuel cells to detonate in a fiery blast. Clicking her tongue, MSI3-5 quickly grabbed hold of her mobile suit's shield and placed it in front of her to keeping the mobile suit's cockpit and torso safe from further damage.

[LIST]"This is getting hectic... almost out of ammo at least, this should be good enough..." muttered the clone, micromanaging not just the actual battle itself, but also whether it had appropriate used all types of missiles and penetrators, whether it had maximized the mobility and propulsion systems of her mobile suit, even basic functions such as accessing the UI and signalling systems under combat to stress test the machine as much as she feasibly could. "Looks like this is it then... urk...!"[/LIST]

Another explosion, this time hitting clean against the shield, causing huge chunks of razor sharp fragments to rain down onto the ground below. An [i]Artillerist[/i], concealed among the multitude of responding military units, had opened fire with a gigantic shell that would blast part of Frame 167's shield into nothingness, exposing its steel backing and badly damaging the mobile suit's left arm, the shield tilting at an awkward angle now, exposing part of the mobile suit's upper chest.

Wary that its time was now running short, MSI3-5 quickly walked back and away from the Illynite onslaught, continuing to open fire with its railgun on the Wardens and tanks, while its rockets would prioritize fighting against the PT boats still hovering in the sky, though only seconds later, both of 167's shoulder-mounted rocket launchers would detonate, self-destructing after running out of ammunition to prevent identification.
